payload.statement: The steward named a design lens after the environmental review: Visual Ecology. The Laboratory should be seen as an environment, not a user interface — each visual object occupies a distinct ecological niche (Architecture, Wayfinding, Annotation, Evidence, History, Invitation, Warning, Ritual, Furniture) and coexists without competing. Consistency makes objects similar; ecology makes them belong. The deeper reading of the earlier repetition finding: the problem was not repetition but niche collision — the History list wears the Annotation species' skin (the taped note), so repeated History spends the Annotation species as wallpaper. Recorded in full as CAB-015. Explicitly a lens, not built from, not ratified.

provenance.intention: record the visual-ecology lens so it survives as a standing way of seeing

payload.conclusion: Adopt Visual Ecology as a standing observational lens, emerging and unratified, that guides how stewardship sees the place but builds nothing until evidence justifies it.
payload.reasoning: Nothing was built from this. The steward asked only to observe and to let ecology become a lens, and the CAB-005 limit forbids encoding a concept into architecture before it is necessary — so the lens is recorded as emerging and non-directive, driving no change. It is the visual counterpart of an existing constitutional principle, that each object owns a distinct responsibility (charter §2), extended from what an object does to what perceptual role it plays. It is held open: whether visual ecology becomes a stated principle of the place is for reality to vote, not for the builder to declare. The lens will classify objects as evidence arrives and will act only when a niche collision is shown to impede a visitor.

provenance.intention: fix the lens's status precisely: a way of seeing, not a mandate to change

payload.statement: The steward offered a further possibility from the ecology lens: a visual object may not be permanently one species but may have a life cycle — its visual identity maturing together with its epistemic maturity. His illustrations: Invitation → Annotation → Evidence → History; and Unknown → Observation → Judgment → Record. The important thought is not the sequences but the coupling of visual identity to epistemic maturity. Held as a possibility only — not built, not adopted, and deliberately NOT turned into another taxonomy, at the steward's instruction. Recorded because it is not foreign to this place: the Constitution already ratifies visual maturation — charter §4, the Journal ages semantically from paper to pencil to ink to typography, so a reader feels the age of an idea before reading it — and the Record's own vocabulary already is a maturity ladder: Unknown, Observation, Judgment, sealed Record. What is not yet coupled is visual identity to that recorded epistemic status. Kept in mind for future evidence; nothing changes now.

provenance.intention: keep the possibility in the Laboratory's memory, since a thought kept only in the builder's head is lost — held, not built
